title: God of My Life, Look Gently Down
description: God of My Life, Look Gently Down in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 39, part 3, headed “Sick-bed devotion; or, Pleading without repining”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God of my life, look gen-tly down, Be-hold the pains I feel; But I am dumb be-fore thy throne, Nor dare dis-pute thy will.

lines: God of my life, look gently down,
But I am dumb before thy throne,
I'll not attempt a murmuring word
Yet I may plead with humble cries,
My strength consumes, my spirit dies
Crush'd as a moth beneath thy hand,
Our feeble powers can ne'er withstand,
Adam and all his numerous race
May I be well prepar'd to go
But if my life be spar'd awhile,
Thy praise shall be my business still,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
